quests.prompt: Write an email to residents' association members notifying them of the upcoming annual general meeting.
options: Subject: Notice of our annual general meeting - 14 october

This year's annual general meeting will take place on 14 october at 7 p.m. in the community hall, where we will review the past year's accounts and vote on two proposed changes to the parking rules - please do try to attend, as we need a minimum number of residents present for votes to count.
quests.hint: The meeting date is central to the subject; all residents are addressed together; the agenda items and a practical reason to attend are in the body; 'KIND REGARDS' closes on behalf of the committee.
quests.explanation: Listing the specific agenda items - accounts and parking rules - helps residents judge whether the meeting is relevant to them. Explaining that a minimum attendance is needed gives people a concrete reason to show up, not just a vague sense of civic duty.

Subject: Nomination for club treasurer - maria santos
quests.hint: The role and nominee's name are in the subject; the secretary is addressed by role, not name; the nominee's relevant experience and confirmed willingness are in the body; the closing must match this unnamed greeting.
quests.explanation: Citing specific, relevant experience ('managed our junior section's budget for two years') makes the nomination substantive rather than just a name put forward. Confirming the nominee has already agreed to stand saves the secretary an unnecessary follow-up step.

quests.explanation: Quoting the exact wording in question ('agreed') pinpoints precisely what needs checking rather than a vague complaint about accuracy. Framing it as your 'recollection' versus their notes, rather than an accusation, keeps the tone collaborative.

quests.prompt: Write an email negotiating the price of a car you are buying privately, based on an issue found during inspection.
options: Subject: Following up after viewing the car

Thank you for showing me the car yesterday - I am still very interested, but my mechanic noticed the front tyres will need replacing soon, so I would like to propose £6,200 instead of the asking price to account for this.
quests.hint: A polite follow-up tone is in the subject; the seller is addressed by name; genuine interest, the specific issue found, and a revised offer are in the body; 'BEST REGARDS' closes the negotiation politely.
quests.explanation: Confirming genuine interest before negotiating reassures the seller this is a real offer, not just haggling. Backing the lower offer with a specific, verifiable reason (worn tyres, found by a mechanic) makes it far harder to dismiss than a round-number discount request.

quests.prompt: Write an email responding to a client's counter-offer on your freelance project quote.
options: Thank you for coming back to me - I can meet you halfway at £680 if we reduce the initial concepts from four to three, which would still give you a strong range to choose from while keeping the project within your budget.

quests.hint: The reply nature is clear in the subject; the client is addressed by name; a genuine compromise on price, paired with a scope adjustment, is in the body; 'BEST REGARDS' closes the negotiation professionally.
quests.explanation: Adjusting the scope (fewer concepts) alongside the price shows the compromise is genuine rather than simply reducing your rate for the same amount of work. Meeting 'halfway' with a specific figure moves the negotiation towards agreement rather than another round of offers.
